questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A VFD trip on overcurrent can be caused by:
questions.solution: Overcurrent trip can result from overload, insulation failure, or mechanical jam.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The ramp time in a VFD refers to:
options: Time to accelerate from 0 to base speed
Both acceleration and deceleration ramp times
questions.solution: Ramp time is the time for speed to change from 0 to maximum (acceleration) or reverse.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: DC injection braking in a VFD is used to:
options: Stop the motor by injecting DC into stator
Run the motor at low speed
questions.solution: DC injection braking stops motor by creating a stationary magnetic field.

questions.stem: The flyback (freewheeling) diode in a DC drive protects against:

questions.solution: Flyback diodes provide path for inductive current when transistors turn off.

questions.stem: The torque ripple in a VFD-fed motor can be reduced by:
questions.solution: Higher PWM frequency smooths current waveform, reducing torque ripple.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The common mode voltage in a VFD can cause:
questions.solution: Common mode voltage causes bearing currents (damage) and EMI.

questions.solution: Thermal model estimates motor temperature to prevent overheating.
